name: old cracked asphalt road of cool charcoal grey with fine scattered non-directional aggregate specks, faded slightly warmer patches, thin crack lines, soft stains and worn broken fragments of yellow and white lane paint, its unconnected edges broken off into dirt as a chipped asphalt lip with loose asphalt chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches (crossroad, dead ends, large slab) with a 1-2 row dark chipped lip along the south edges

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain sheet: a speckled brown dirt ground with grey asphalt road shapes laid on it. The asphalt shapes are seen straight down. Their only vertical cue is a 1-2 row dark chipped lip along the south edges (e.g. rows 61, 125 and the underside of the large slab), which is a rim and not a front face of 3 or more rows. There is no receding side face and no eave. The ground fills the full 192 rows, so there is no standing volume and no separate front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt reads as 3 close grey steps (body, darker speckle, dark edge) with a few thin crack lines. Beodeul paving has about 5-7 visible tones, with a lit edge, a shaded edge and stones shaded one by one. The candidate has 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 for paving and 3 for grass, so the measure is comparable. Near-flat coverage is 5%, so the fills are not large. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the lip is tinted, but the asphalt edge is only a thin dark rim and the soil beside it is also brown. The lane paint is a tiny yellow dash and the white paint is barely visible, so the worn paint fragments are mostly missing. The asphalt patches look like flat grey stickers laid on brown soil with no chipped lip highlight and little loose-chunk detail. The 4x3 network is also sparse, with isolated blobs rather than a connected network with crossroads, so it is thinner and flatter than the reference. A careful artist would not accept it beside the Beodeul paving.

styleAnswer.evidence: The whole candidate uses only 13 distinct colours, split between the dirt and the asphalt. The asphalt ramp is shallow: a mid charcoal base, a lighter speck, a darker speck and a dark edge, so about 3 steps against the references' 5-6. The dirt shows mottling in about 3-4 tones. The measured 5 visible tones per tile sit below the paving reference (7) and above the grass (3). Near-flat coverage is 5%, so the speckle does break up the fill, but it is a uniform non-directional dot scatter with no per-chunk shading. The edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans toward the adjacent material (brownish dark) rather than black. The brief asks for warmer faded patches, soft stains, cracks and worn lane paint. The cracks are only a few thin dark lines and the yellow paint is one tiny dash, so these details barely register. The chipped lip and loose chunks are blobby silhouettes with little internal shading. Overall it reads thinner and flatter than the paving reference, so I fail it narrowly under the 'when in doubt, fail' rule.
